source: Frank W. Gould (1975), The Grasses of Texas

option.label: Male and female flowers in separate spikelets
option.detail: Check each spikelet, not just whether the entire plant bears both sexes.

option.label: LOWER branches male; UPPER branches female
option.detail: Texas wildrice: lower branches have awnless male spikelets; upper branches long-awned female spikelets.

option.label: On a branch: female below, male above
option.detail: Southern wildrice: male and female spikelets share branches, with male spikelets above.

option.label: True glumes absent; irregular basal cup may remain
option.detail: Texas wildrice has no conventional paired glumes; distinguish any irregular disarticulation cup from glumes.

option.label: FEMALE flower: one hard lemma, no palea
option.detail: Southern wildrice female organ only; male flower has a separate palea.

option.label: Rachilla joints without hairs
option.detail: Inspect the small axis between florets. Giant reed has silky lemma-base hairs but a hairless rachilla.

option.label: Lemma nerves or surface rough (not necessarily hairy)
option.detail: Scabrous nerves are not proof of conspicuous long hairs.

option.label: Brome lemma awns spread apart at maturity
option.detail: Japanese brome awns become divergent and contorted near the base; lowest may remain erect.

observations.habit: Small tufted perennial, occasionally appearing annual; slender spreading stems commonly 3–10 cm, exceptionally 2–15 cm. Basal branching; flowering stems initially enclosed by leaf sheaths.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths often have long hairs at base; approximately 0.5-mm membrane with fine marginal cilia. Blades rather stiff, commonly 1–1.5 mm wide; flat to inrolled, glabrous or rough.
observations.flowers: Spikelets commonly 7–15 mm, 6–12-flowered. Unequal pointed glumes; first 1–2 nerves, second 3 nerves and shorter than florets. Lemmas 3–5 mm, densely rough, especially on keel; acute, sometimes ending in a short straight or curved awn. Short lemmas pubescent between nerves; palea keels broadly winged.
observations.context: Flowering June–November; footer absent in crop, so no printed page is invented.

evidence.note: Mostly 1–1.5 mm; not a measured local specimen.
Glabrous/scabrous blade wording; do not infer blade hairs from sheath.
Very short ciliate membrane; keep existing hair-fringe interpretation as separately sourced.
Short straight/curved awn only sometimes present.

cautions: Printed page not visible; evidence kept as page-unconfirmed and non-excluding. Existing current-name crosswalk retained, not reclassified from an image.

SOURCE DIFFERENCE / PAGE HOLD: Gould describes an approximately 0.5-mm finely ciliate membrane; earlier sources differ over hair fringe versus membrane and ligule length. The supplied crop lacks its footer. Preserve these distinctions and do not create a new exclusion.

observations.habit: Aquatic fleshy perennial; decumbent or stolon-like basal stems root at lower nodes, with erect portions mostly 1–1.7 m; stems hairless.
observations.collar_blade: Membranous ligule 5–15 mm; blades thin and flat, mostly about 1.4 cm wide.
observations.flowers: Panicle mostly 20–30 cm. Lower spreading branches bear awnless one-flowered male spikelets and may droop with age; upper upright branches bear long-awned one-flowered female spikelets. Male spikelets mostly 7–9 mm with thin 5-veined awnless lemmas. Female spikelets about 1 cm excluding a curved awn 1–2 cm long; lemma leathery, 7-veined, tapering into a hairy beak, palea faintly 3-veined. Apparent glumes absent apart from an irregular cup or membrane at disarticulation.
observations.context: Gould restricts known occurrence to spring-fed, fast clear fresh water of the San Marcos River near its source. April–November, irregular flowering. This historical account does not establish present range or a new voucher.

evidence.note: Distinguish basal posture from erect flowering portion.
Each sex has separate one-flowered spikelets.
Lower branches male; upper branches female.
Do not confuse the irregular basal cup with conventional glumes.
Long female lemma awn; male lemma awnless. Never require both on one spikelet.

cautions: SOURCE CONFLICT IN THE COMPARISON: the earlier giant-cutgrass comparison below puts females nearer branch tips and mentions a short female awn. Gould p.49 instead puts male Zizaniopsis above female and describes awnless spikelets. Do not transfer that disputed comparison onto Texas wildrice.

observations.habit: Coarse perennial with rhizomes and thick glabrous stems, generally 2–3 m.
observations.collar_blade: Membranous ligules with many fine nerves, mostly 6–20 mm; hairless blades mostly 8–22 mm wide and 1 m or longer.
observations.flowers: Erect-spreading, freely branching panicle 30–60 cm, occasionally longer. Male and female spikelets on the same branches, male above female. Male spikelets 3–10 mm, awnless; thin 7-nerved lemma and thin 3-nerved palea; disarticulation just below glumes. Female spikelets awnless with a single hardened lemma and no palea, persistent on mature fruit. Grain glossy/globose, about 3 mm, crowned by central style and two small projections.
observations.context: Shallow water at stream/lake margins; mostly April–July, occasionally later. Keep historical range and sex/disarticulation wording source-specific.

evidence.note: Rhizomatous without a stated runner length.
One-flowered male and female spikelets; organs differ by sex.
On the same branch, male spikelets above female.
Female flower has one hardened lemma, no palea. Do not apply this to male flower.

cautions: SOURCE CONFLICT: Gould p.49 places male spikelets ABOVE female on the same branch and calls both sexes awnless. Earlier supplementary checks describe the opposite order and a short female awn. These competing statements remain recorded; Gould is the controlling book here, and this batch adds no new hard exclusions.

observations.habit: Slender rhizomatous perennial, stems mostly 80–150 cm, often decumbent or stolon-like. Nodes point-hairy; sheaths usually strongly rough.
observations.collar_blade: Short firm truncate ligule. Flat thin firm blades mostly 7–10 mm wide and 10–20 cm long, often partly enclosed by upper sheath. Blade margins/midrib sharply serrate and scabrous.
observations.flowers: Slender lower branches of the panicle bear spikelets in basal 1–3.5 cm. Spikelets narrowly oblong and asymmetric; lemma and palea short-hairy or rough, often rough-hairy at keels.
observations.context: May–November, mostly autumn; shallow lakes, rivers and marshes. No rhizome length inferred.

evidence.note: Lemma/palea short-hairy or scabrous; do not replace roughness with mandatory long hairs.

observations.habit: Rhizomatous perennial; largely unbranched culms up to 1.5 m, leaves along most of stem.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths glabrous, often reddish-purple; throat and collar long-haired. Ciliate membrane about 1 mm or less. Blades thin flat glabrous or slightly hairy near ligule, mostly 1–2 cm wide, gradually narrowed at both ends.
observations.flowers: Open inflorescence with drooping branches; flat, many-flowered, awnless spikelets on slender pedicels. Panicle axis/branches/pedicels often drooping. Spikelets mostly 1–1.6(–2) cm broad and 1.6–2(–2.6) cm long, sharply keeled laterally compressed lemmas. Lower 1–2 florets neuter. Glumes 5–7 mm, subequal, acute, 5–7-veined. Lemmas entire or bifid, 11–15-veined; hairy keel extends from base to apex.
observations.context: June–October; shaded wooded banks and stream bottoms. Only terminal portion of genus key is in this image.

evidence.note: About 1 mm or less, boundary retained.
Blades glabrous or slightly pilose near ligule.
Both glumes 5–7-nerved; existing upper-specific choice valid.

observations.habit: Perennial reed with stout stems commonly 2–6 m from thick knotty rhizomes; culms and leaves glabrous.
observations.collar_blade: Leaves uniformly spaced on stem; rounded sheaths. Ciliate membrane about 1 mm or less. Thick flat elongate sharply tapering blades mostly 4–7 cm wide, rough at margins.
observations.flowers: Dense many-flowered panicle generally 30–60 cm and half as broad, with spreading branches; branches/branchlets glabrous or nearly so. Spikelets mostly 2–4-flowered, 10–15 mm and short-stalked; rachilla joints hairless. Glumes broad, thin, almost equal, irregularly nerved and narrowly pointed. Lemmas thin, 3–5-veined, 5–10 mm, long silky-hairy at base; apex short-awned or pointed, and awn/glabrous distal third has a small tooth on each side.
observations.context: Mostly September–November. Keep lemma basal hairs distinct from the hairless rachilla; no species/lineage diagnosis inferred from reed silhouette alone.

evidence.note: Long silky hairs at lemma base.
Short-awned or pointed apex; retain conditional distinction.

observations.habit: Stout perennial; culms 2–4 m from thick creeping rhizomes, with stolons also often produced. Culms/leaves glabrous.
observations.collar_blade: Leafy culms, no inflorescence-base sheath. Ciliate ligule membrane with hairs longer than membrane base. Flat elongate blades, rough margins, mostly 1.5–5.5 cm wide.
observations.flowers: Dense panicle, ovoid to lance-shaped, branches many-rebranched but contracted. Disarticulation above glumes and between florets. Spikelets 10–15 mm, usually 4–8-flowered. Rachilla joints long-hairy, hairs 6–8 mm; lemmas and paleas hairless. First glume half to two-thirds second; 3–5-nerved, acute/mucronate. Lowest floret infertile, lemma mostly 11–14 mm and much longer than upper lemmas.
observations.context: July–November, sometimes throughout year. Gould describes the broad historical species and notes competing communis/australis usage. This does not identify native/introduced North American lineage.

evidence.note: Ciliate membrane; cilia longer than base.
Long hairs on rachilla joints, not lemma.

cautions: Do not assign lineage, county nativity or invasive status from this broad account.

observations.habit: Perennial with a firm, often woody rhizomatous base; culms mostly 50–120 cm, tufted.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths hairless, rough or short-hairy, closed nearly to apex. Ligules mostly 3–6 mm. Blades glabrous, scabrous or short-hairy, flat, 3–10(–15) mm wide; 10–26 cm on longer stems, sometimes shorter.
observations.flowers: Panicle branches commonly compound, spreading/ascending. Spikelets with 1–4, usually 2–3, fertile florets, not spreading and slightly shorter than at maturity. Glumes shorter than spikelet, obtuse or acute, membranous, rough margins; first usually broad 5–7 mm, second similar narrower 7–9 mm. Lemmas striate, finely rugose/scabrous; 11 nerves with hyaline margins and awnless apex. Anthers 3–5 mm. Distal rudiment oblong/ovate, rarely broadly based near apex, erect and not spreading away from rachilla.
observations.context: Mostly April–June; rocky slopes, open woodland and stream banks.

evidence.note: Woody rhizomatous base, not proof of long runners.
1–4 fertile florets, usually 2–3, plus distal rudiment.

observations.habit: Tufted perennial; stems mostly 30–70(–90) cm, often knee-bent and spreading at base. Nodes usually pressed-hairy, losing hairs with age.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths variously hairy or nearly glabrous, margins ciliate and collar long-haired. Ligules variable: absent/minute to thin truncate/erose membrane up to 1 mm. Blades 10–30(–40) cm, 1–4(–6) mm, pilose or hispid both sides, flat or closely inrolled.
observations.flowers: Panicle mostly 6–25 cm, initially enclosed in sheaths, later open with long slender flexuous branches. Glumes thin, glabrous, attenuate; second 14–18 mm, first three- or five-veined, second five-veined. Sharp densely hairy callus; lemma 9–12 mm, densely hairy below, rough toward apex with projecting hairs at neck. Floret apex contracted into a 0.5–1 mm crown. Lemma awn 4.5–10 cm, commonly 6–10, usually twice bent and twisted in lower part.
observations.context: Mostly March–May, occasionally later in cool sites. Ligule absence is explicit variation, not absence inferred from silence.

evidence.note: Hair variable, long hairs at collar.
Present membranes reach 1 mm; absence retained separately in existing core.
Dense callus hairs are not a rachilla beard.
Awn 45–100 mm, lower segment twisted, commonly twice bent.

species.taxon_as_printed: Bromus unioloides; Gould discussion compares B. catharticus

observations.habit: Annual in Texas, tufted, mostly 50–80 cm, tending to flatten laterally and with some keel.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths nearly hairless to densely short-hairy; margins finely strigose. Ligules mostly 3–4 mm, developed; blades mostly 5–12 mm, broad, glabrous or hirsute with spreading hairs, thin in Texas flowering plants.
observations.flowers: Open drooping panicle of large flattened spikelets with 6–12 florets. First glume mostly 5–7-nerved, second mostly 7–9-nerved. Lemmas 7–11-nerved, laterally flattened and sharply keeled, slightly scabrous/pubescent or glabrous, with awn 1–3 mm or none.
observations.context: Early spring–early summer. Gould reports plants called B. unioloides and distinguishes older B. catharticus nomenclature. Kew POWO lists Bromus unioloides Kunth as a synonym of B. catharticus; Gould also explicitly discusses the Hitchcock name usage. Retain historical concept warning.

cautions: Historical B. unioloides crosswalk supported by Kew POWO https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:315500-2 and Gould discussion; no merger with other brome species.

observations.habit: Short-lived annual; culms usually 40–75 cm, laterally flattened, firm and somewhat flexible.
observations.collar_blade: Blades thin 3–7 mm, uniformly short-hairy both surfaces, sometimes longer-haired below. Sheaths short-hairy. Ligules 1–1.7 mm.
observations.flowers: Narrow panicle or raceme 10–15 cm. Spikelets nearly cylindrical, becoming broader at flowering, 2 cm or less, 6–8 florets. First glume 1-nerved, second 3-nerved, usually both membranous and glabrous/scabrous. Lemmas mostly 7–9 mm with 6–10 mm awn.
observations.context: Spring. Sticky/bluish mold on seedheads is reported context, not a mandatory identification character.

evidence.note: First 1-veined; second 3-veined. Glabrous or scabrous glumes.
True lemma awn 6–10 mm; generic short option has no fixed threshold.

observations.habit: Perennial; culms mostly 70–140 cm. Lower sheaths densely pilose, with spreading hairs; upper sheaths short-hairy or glabrous.
observations.collar_blade: Blades mostly 5–10 mm broad, glabrous or less often sparsely hirsute.
observations.flowers: Panicle usually 10–25 cm, erect/spreading or spreading-recurved branches; lower branches can be 8 cm. Spikelets mostly 2–3.5 cm, 5–12 florets. Glumes sparse-hirsute, first 1-veined, second 3–5-veined. Lemmas rounded on back, glabrous or less often inconspicuously hirsute, with 5–11 mm awn.
observations.context: Spring. Gould discusses B. nottowayanus separation as not justified for the Texas material; this historical remark does not automatically merge unrelated current profiles.

evidence.note: Dense spreading hairs on lower sheaths; upper sheaths short-hairy or glabrous.
Rounded back; mostly hairless, occasional fine hirsute.

cautions: SOURCE DIFFERENCE: Gould p.87 calls lemmas usually glabrous, occasionally inconspicuously hirsute, with 5–11 mm awns. Earlier supplementary checks describe denser interveinal hairs and 3–8 mm awns. Retain the ranges and hair variation separately; hairs are not mandatory.

species.taxon_as_printed: Bromus tectorum, including var. tectorum and var. glabratus

observations.habit: Annual with weak erect/spreading culms, usually 25–60 cm.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths/blades usually softly hairy but sometimes nearly hairless. Blades typically 2.5–5 mm.
observations.flowers: Loose drooping panicle, branches/pedicels slender and flexuous, often S-curved. Spikelets mostly 1–2 cm excluding awns, usually 4–6 florets. Unequal glumes: first narrow 1-veined, second nearly twice as long and 3-veined. Lower lemmas mostly 9–12 mm, scabrous on nerves and slender apical teeth, awn 9–18 mm. Var. tectorum has hirsute/pubescent lemmas; var. glabratus has glabrous/scabrous lemmas.
observations.context: Spring–early summer; varieties not separate current profiles. Do not make hairy lemmas mandatory across both varieties.

evidence.note: First one vein, second three and almost twice as long.
Awn 9–18 mm, qualify numeric range rather than universal length threshold.

observations.habit: Annual; slender spreading culms mostly 30–60 cm.
observations.collar_blade: Sheaths at least lowermost typically densely pilose with soft spreading or reflexed hairs. Blades glabrous or short-hairy, mostly 2–7 mm.
observations.flowers: Panicle 8–20 cm, slender spreading flexuous often kinked branches/pedicels. Spikelets 1.5–3 cm excluding awns, 6–11 florets. First glume 3–5-nerved, second 5–9-nerved. Lemmas 7–9 mm, conspicuous broad rounded/obtuse marginal angles near apex. Mature lemmas fold inward with grain nearly as broad as long. Awn mostly 8–12 mm, contorted at base and divergent at maturity. Lower lemma awns may stay erect.
observations.context: Spring. Page 92–93 discussion distinguishes it from B. secalinus using hairs, lemma-tooth shape and mature awn spread. Do not apply the neighboring secalinus description to japonicus.

evidence.note: Awn 8–12 mm, base contorted; spreading at maturity, lowest can remain straight.

secondary_review: Existing Diggs/Hagenbuch/FNA evidence remains attached. This batch directly rereads supplied Gould accounts; it does not claim new direct rereads of unavailable secondary pages. All state additions are positive-only; disagreements retain earlier sources.

Phyllostachys aurea: no confirmed species account supplied.
